limitations_and_boundaries: Biolord suffers from lack of direct interpretability of the deep generative framework, though downstream analysis tools provide biological insight in feature space.
When attributes are correlated, predictions over unseen combinations may yield unpredictable results, a known limitation of neural networks.

research_questions.statement: How can single-cell multi-omic data be disentangled into known and unknown attributes to enable counterfactual predictions and biological discovery?

provenance.text_excerpt: We show that biolord outperforms GEARS in the prediction of unseen one-gene perturbation (normalized mean squared error, one of one gene unseen; GEARS: 0.47; biolord: 0.37) and two-gene perturbations (normalized mean squared error, two of two genes unseen; GEARS: 0.53; biolord: 0.50, one of one gene unseen; GEARS: 0.39; biolord: 0.35, zero of two genes unseen; GEARS: 0.28; biolord: 0.20; Methods; Supplementary Note 3 and Extended Data Fig. 2).

claims.statement: Biolord outperforms GEARS in predicting unseen one-gene and two-gene genetic perturbations on Perturb-seq datasets.

provenance.text_excerpt: Biolord’s learned latent representation is biologically informative; it reveals drug organization according to known corresponding pathways, and better captures underlying drug organization, relative to the chemically informed RDKit features used as input, both qualitatively and quantitatively (adjusted Rand index RDKit: 0.03, biolord: 0.16; Supplementary Fig. 4). To further evaluate the quality of biolord’s drugs representation, we employ the uncertainty measure suggested by ref. 5, assessing the ability to predict the drug’s pathway from the k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) graph of the embedding space (Methods). Compared to RDKit, biolord’s uncertainty measure is found to be lower on average and more concentrated (distribution evaluated over all drugs; RDKit: 0.32±0.008, biolord: 0.19±0.005; Supplementary Fig. 4).

claims.statement: Biolord's learned drug latent space is more biologically informative than input RDKit features, with higher adjusted Rand index (0.16 vs 0.03) and lower uncertainty (0.19 vs 0.32).

provenance.text_excerpt: Biolord also outperforms PerturbNet8 (Supplementary Note 3) and is robust to data subsampling, retaining high prediction accuracy (mean r2: 0.63±0.0003) over 10% of the data (Supplementary Fig. 5).

claims.statement: Biolord robustly predicts unseen drug responses even with 10% of training data (r2 = 0.63).

provenance.text_excerpt: Biolord outperforms a naive baseline (comparing real measurements of unseen compounds to the control measurements), as well as state-of-the-art models, chemCPA and chemCPA-pre (Fig. 1e, Supplementary Fig. 4 and Supplementary Note 3). Although not provided with the additional information used by chemCPA-pre, biolord provides more accurate predictions (mean r2; chemCPA-pre: 0.51 ± 0.0062, biolord: 0.76 ± 0.0005).

claims.statement: Biolord outperforms chemCPA and chemCPA-pre in predicting unseen drug responses on the sci-Plex 3 dataset, achieving r2 = 0.76 vs 0.51 for chemCPA-pre.

evidence_spans.content: Biolord is a deep generative method for disentangling single-cell multi-omic data to known and unknown attributes, including spatial, temporal and disease states, used to reveal the decoupled biological signatures over diverse single-cell modalities and biological systems.

provenance.text_excerpt: Biolord is a deep generative method for disentangling single-cell multi-omic data to known and unknown attributes, including spatial, temporal and disease states, used to reveal the decoupled biological signatures over diverse single-cell modalities and biological systems.

evidence_spans.content: Counterfactual predictions using biolord on Plasmodium infection data revealed an increase in expression of immune and stress pathway genes in infected hepatocytes, consistent with prior reports.

provenance.text_excerpt: We use the trained biolord model to obtain counterfactual predictions for nine unseen drugs (reported among the most effective drugs in sci-Plex 3 data16, following the choice suggested in ref. 5). Specifically, we generate the expression prediction for control cells with labels of unseen compounds. Performance is evaluated using the r2 score between the real measurements of cells exposed to the unseen compounds and the counterfactual predictions (Fig. 1d; Methods). Biolord outperforms a naive baseline (comparing real measurements of unseen compounds to the control measurements), as well as state-of-the-art models, chemCPA and chemCPA-pre (Fig. 1e, Supplementary Fig. 4 and Supplementary Note 3).

experiments_or_tasks: Counterfactual analysis of Plasmodium infection progression in mouse liver at single-cell level.
Prediction of cellular responses to unseen drugs using sci-Plex 3 dataset (649,340 cells, 7,561 genes, three cancer cell lines, 188 drugs at four dosages).

Prediction of unseen one-gene and two-gene genetic perturbations using Perturb-seq datasets (one-gene: 65,899 cells, 5,060 genes, 81 perturbations; two-gene: 89,357 cells, 5,045 genes, 131 two-gene and 105 one-gene perturbations).
Semi-supervised classification of abortive hepatocytes in Plasmodium infection data using biolord-classify.

methods.name: Biolord
methods.protocol_description: Deep generative framework with decomposed latent space: each known attribute (categorical or ordered) has a dedicated subnetwork (embeddings for categorical, MLP encoder for ordered), unknown attributes use per-sample embedding with Gaussian noise and L2 regularization. Generator (decoder) outputs distribution parameters (Gaussian, ZINB, or Poisson) from concatenated latent codes. Trained with completeness loss (negative log-likelihood + MSE) and minimality loss (L2 penalty on unknown embedding). Hyperparameters tuned via Weights & Biases.

methods.name: Biolord-classify
methods.protocol_description: Extends biolord with classifiers (cross-entropy) for categorical attributes and regressors (MSE) for ordered attributes, trained jointly to impute missing labels. Classification loss added to biolord objective.
